reasoning_summary:
Context: this is the corollary subpage of Schur's Lemma, so the parent hypothesis that V is an irreducible (simple) G-module is inherited; without it the statement is false (V = k^2 with trivial action gives End_G V = M_2(k)). Read with that inherited hypothesis, every step is justified. Note also that finite-dimensionality of V is not needed as an extra assumption: a simple k[G]-module for finite G is cyclic, hence a quotient of k[G], hence dim V <= |G| < infinity, and V != 0 by simplicity, so characteristic polynomials and eigenvalues exist.
0001 Justified: notation only, I_V is the identity map on V.
0003 Justified: the zero endomorphism is 0*I_V and 0 lies in k, so the f = 0 case is already of the required scalar form.
0005 Justified but elided: this opens the complementary case. Exhaustiveness (every nonzero f in End_G V is an automorphism) is exactly Schur's Lemma for the simple module V, cited later at 0021 but not invoked here; the gap is standard and fillable from the lemma the proof already uses.
0007 Justified: k algebraically closed is a hypothesis of the problem.
0009 Justified: over an algebraically closed field every polynomial in k[x] splits into linear factors, so the characteristic polynomial of f (which exists since dim V is finite, as argued above) is completely reducible.
0011 Justified: the roots of the split characteristic polynomial are the eigenvalues, and they all lie in k; V != 0 guarantees at least one exists.
0013 Justified: fixes such an eigenvalue, legitimate by 0011.
0015-0016 Justified: f - lambda*I_V is a linear endomorphism of V, and it is a G-module homomorphism since f is one and scalar multiples of the identity commute with the G-action (this last point is left implicit but is immediate).
0018-0019 Justified: by definition of eigenvalue there is a nonzero v with f(v) = lambda*v, so ker(f - lambda*I_V) != {0}.
0021-0022 Justified: f - lambda*I_V is a G-endomorphism of the simple module V with nonzero kernel, hence not injective, hence not an isomorphism; Schur's Lemma then forces it to be 0, i.e. f = lambda*I_V. This is the crux and it is correct under the inherited irreducibility hypothesis.
0024 Justified: (lambda I_V) o (mu I_V) = (lambda mu) I_V is a direct computation on each vector.
0026 Justified: lambda I_V + (-mu I_V) = (lambda - mu) I_V, likewise pointwise.
0028-0029 Justified: by 0003 and 0022 every element of End_G V is scalar times I_V; the set is nonempty (contains I_V) and, by 0024 and 0026, closed under subtraction and composition, so the Subring Test applies inside End(V) as an abelian group.
0031-0032 Justified: phi(lambda I_V) = lambda is well defined because V != 0 makes lambda I_V = mu I_V force lambda = mu; the map is defined on all of End_G V by 0029. (Minor cosmetic issue: phi already names the G-action in the problem statement.)
0035 Justified: additivity follows from 0026 (with -mu replaced by mu).
0036 Justified: multiplicativity follows from 0024; phi(I_V) = 1 also holds.
0038 Justified but elided: the homomorphism property is what 0035-0036 show; bijectivity is not spelled out, but surjectivity is immediate since every lambda in k yields lambda I_V in End_G V, and injectivity is the well-definedness argument in reverse (V != 0). Fillable in one line.
0040 Justified: End_G V is ring-isomorphic to the field k, and being a field is preserved under ring isomorphism, so End_G V is a field with the same structure as k, which is the claimed conclusion.
Overall: no step is mathematically false; the only defects are routine elisions (case exhaustiveness at 0005, bijectivity at 0038, and the unstated inheritance of irreducibility/finite-dimensionality), all of which are closable from results the proof itself cites.
